parameters.content:
## Workflow A · Loan product discovery
Runs daily. Crawls **BankBazaar** two levels deep (rate table -> one eligibility page per bank), plus **Tata Capital** (lender) and **Paisabazaar** (marketplace).

**Cost control:** each page's cleaned text is hashed. If the hash matches the last crawl, the LLM is skipped entirely, so a normal day with no website changes makes **zero** LLM calls.

The LLM turns each changed page into numeric rules (income, score, age, employment) that Workflow B can match with plain SQL. Only rules that cannot be numbers go into `eligibility_notes`.

parameters.query: SELECT (SELECT content_hash FROM source_pages WHERE url = $1) AS previous_hash

-- One statement: record the page's new hash, upsert its products, and retire
-- products that this page used to list but no longer does.
WITH page AS (
  INSERT INTO source_pages (url, site, content_hash, product_count, last_crawled_at, last_changed_at)
  VALUES ($1, $2, $3, jsonb_array_length($4::jsonb), now(), now())
  ON CONFLICT (url) DO UPDATE SET
    content_hash = EXCLUDED.content_hash, product_count = EXCLUDED.product_count,
    last_crawled_at = now(), last_changed_at = now()
  RETURNING url
),
incoming AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($4::jsonb) AS p(
    lender text, product_name text, interest_rate_min numeric, interest_rate_max numeric,
    min_monthly_income numeric, min_credit_score int, max_credit_score int,
    min_age int, max_age int, allowed_employment text[], eligibility_notes text)
),
upserted AS (
  INSERT INTO loan_products (lender, product_name, source_url, interest_rate_min, interest_rate_max,
    min_monthly_income, min_credit_score, max_credit_score, min_age, max_age,
    allowed_employment, eligibility_notes, is_active, last_seen_at, updated_at)
  SELECT lender, product_name, (SELECT url FROM page), interest_rate_min, interest_rate_max,
    min_monthly_income, min_credit_score, max_credit_score, min_age, max_age,
    allowed_employment, eligibility_notes, true, now(), now()
  FROM incoming
  ON CONFLICT (lender, product_name) DO UPDATE SET
    source_url = EXCLUDED.source_url,
    interest_rate_min = EXCLUDED.interest_rate_min, interest_rate_max = EXCLUDED.interest_rate_max,
    min_monthly_income = EXCLUDED.min_monthly_income,
    min_credit_score = EXCLUDED.min_credit_score, max_credit_score = EXCLUDED.max_credit_score,
    min_age = EXCLUDED.min_age, max_age = EXCLUDED.max_age,
    allowed_employment = EXCLUDED.allowed_employment, eligibility_notes = EXCLUDED.eligibility_notes,
    is_active = true, last_seen_at = now(), updated_at = now()
  RETURNING product_id
),
retired AS (
  UPDATE loan_products SET is_active = false, updated_at = now()
  WHERE source_url = $1 AND is_active AND product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM upserted)
  RETURNING product_id
)
SELECT $1 AS url, (SELECT count(*) FROM upserted) AS products_saved, (SELECT count(*) FROM retired) AS products_retired

-- Unchanged page: no LLM call. Just record that we looked, and keep its products alive.
WITH touched AS (
  UPDATE source_pages SET last_crawled_at = now() WHERE url = $1 RETURNING url
)
-- (A failed fetch does not count as "seen", so a page that stays down retires its products.)
UPDATE loan_products SET last_seen_at = now() WHERE source_url = $1 AND NOT $2::boolean
RETURNING product_id

-- After the loop: products not found by any crawl for 7 days are switched off,
-- so users are never matched against a loan that has disappeared.
WITH retired AS (
  UPDATE loan_products SET is_active = false, updated_at = now()
  WHERE is_active AND last_seen_at < now() - interval '7 days'
  RETURNING product_id
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM retired) AS retired,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM loan_products WHERE is_active) AS active_products,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM source_pages WHERE last_crawled_at > now() - interval '1 hour') AS pages_crawled
